'''Galen D. Stucky''' (born 17 December 1936) is an American inorganic materials chemist who is a Distinguished Professor and the Essam Khashoggi Chair In Materials Chemistry at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name=":2" /> He is noted for his work with porous ordered mesoporous materials such as [[Mesoporous silica|SBA-15]]. He won the Prince of Asturias Award in 2014, in the Scientific and Technological Research area. Stucky was elected a member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1994,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cohen|first=Julie|date=September 25, 2014|title=Another List of Laureates|url=https://www.news.ucsb.edu/2014/014410/another-list-laureates|access-date=2021-06-05|website=The UCSB Current|language=en}}</ref> a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2005,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Galen D. Stucky|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/galen-d-stucky|access-date=2021-06-05|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|last=Fernandez|first=Sonia|date=April 30, 2013|title=UCSB Professor Galen Stucky Elected to National Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.news.ucsb.edu/2013/013516/uc-santa-barbara-professor-galen-stucky-elected-national-academy-sciences|website=The UCSB Current}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Galen D. Stucky|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/galen-d-stucky-qytthj/|access-date=2021-06-05|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Stucky was born on December 17, 1936, in [[McPherson, Kansas|McPherson]], [[Kansas]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Cheetham |first1=Anthony K. |last2=Eckert |first2=Hellmut |last3=Rao |first3=C.N.R. |title=Galen D. Stucky on the Occasion of his 65th Birthday |journal=Journal of Solid State Chemistry |date=September 2002 |volume=167 |issue=2 |pages=265–266 |doi=10.1006/jssc.2002.9726 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Stucky |first=Galen D. |title=Molecular Configurations of Some of the Solvated Compounds of the Grignard System |date=1962 |degree=Ph.D. |id={{ProQuest|288095659}}}}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref> He graduated with a Bachelor's of Science degree at [[McPherson College]] in 1957.<ref name=":0" /> Stucky pursued graduate studies at [[Iowa State University]], where he worked under Prof. [[Robert E. Rundle]] on the synthesis and characterization of the [[diethyl ether]]-solvated [[phenylmagnesium bromide]] [[Grignard reagent]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stucky |first1=Galen D. |last2=Rundle |first2=R. E. |title=The Structure of Phenylmagnesium Bromide Dietherate and the Nature of Grignard Reagents |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=April 1963 |volume=85 |issue=7 |pages=1002–1003 |doi=10.1021/ja00890a039 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stucky |first1=G. |last2=Rundle |first2=R. E. |title=The Constitution of the Grignard Reagent, Phenylmagnesium Bromide Dietherate |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=November 1964 |volume=86 |issue=22 |pages=4825–4830 |doi=10.1021/ja01076a020 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref> and an oxidation product formed from its exposure to oxygen.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stucky |first1=G. |last2=Rundle |first2=R. E. |title=The Crystal and Molecular Structure of Mg<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>6</sub>O·4C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>O, a Grignard Reagent Oxidation Product |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=November 1964 |volume=86 |issue=22 |pages=4821–4825 |doi=10.1021/ja01076a019 }}{{psc|date=February 2024}}</ref> Stucky received his PhD in physical chemistry in 1962.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Galen Stucky {{!}} Department of Chemistry - UC Santa Barbara|url=https://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/galen-stucky|access-date=2021-06-05|website=www.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en}}</ref> From 1962 to 1963, he was a postdoctoral associate in the Department of Physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under Prof. [[Clifford Shull|Clifford G. Shull]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Stucky began his independent academic career in 1964 as an assistant professor at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] (UIUC), and was promoted to full professor in 1972.<ref name=":0" /> In 1980, he left UIUC to work at Sandia National Laboratory in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico|Albuquerque]], [[New Mexico]], where he led the Solid State Materials Group there.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Stucky Group Biography|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/stucky/galen/stuckygroup/biography.html|access-date=2021-06-05|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu}}</ref> From 1981 to 1985, he worked at the [[DuPont Central Research|Central Research and Development Laboratory]] of [[E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Co.]] in [[Wilmington, Delaware|Wilmington]], [[Delaware]], where he was a group and research leader.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In 1985, Stucky joined the faculty of the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. He is the E. Khashoggi Industries, LLC Professor in Letters and Science, Professor in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry (College of Letters and Science), Professor in the Materials Department (College of Engineering), and a member of the Interdepartmental Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Stucky Group: Home at UCSB|url=http://www.chem.ucsb.edu/~stuckygroup/stuckygroup/|access-date=December 17, 2011|publisher=Chem.ucsb.edu}}</ref>

==Notability==
Stucky has been ranked in the top five most-cited materials scientists in the world, according to [[Thomson Scientific]]'s in-cites publication (more than 80 publications with over 60 citations).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://in-cites.com/top/2007/second07-mat-sci.html |title=Second Bimonthly Period of 2007 – Top 10 Researchers In Materials Science |publisher=in-cites |access-date=December 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080307143134/http://in-cites.com/top/2007/second07-mat-sci.html |archive-date=March 7, 2008 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> According to another publication by Thomson in late 2006, his work involving [[Mesoporous silica|SBA]] was the most-cited paper in the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.in-cites.com/research/2006/november_20_2006-1.html |title=SCI-BYTES: Top Ten Most-Cited Journals (All Fields), 1996–2006 |publisher=In-cites.com |access-date=December 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090609175102/http://www.in-cites.com/research/2006/november_20_2006-1.html |archive-date=June 9, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> In 2007 his [[Hirsch index]] rating ranked in the top 40 among living chemists,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/News/2007/April/23040701.asp |title=H-index ranking of living chemists |publisher=Rsc.org |access-date=December 17, 2011}}</ref>  and he was ranked in the top 30 most-cited scientists in chemistry by in-cites in late 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://in-cites.com/nobel/2007-che-top100.html |title=Most-Cited Scientists in Chemistry (Jan 97 – Jun 07) |publisher=In-cites.com |access-date=December 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090604122232/http://in-cites.com/nobel/2007-che-top100.html |archive-date=June 4, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> In June 2008, [[Institute for Scientific Information|Sciencewatch.com]] featured "Mesoporous Materials" as a Special Topics analysis publication.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sciencewatch.com/ana/st/mes-mat/ |title=Mesoporous Materials, Special Topics, sciencewatch.com, June 2008 |publisher=Sciencewatch.com |date=February 29, 2008 |access-date=December 17, 2011}}</ref> He contributed research in the development of [[QuikClot]], a lifesaving blood clotting drug with military and civilian applications.<ref>{{cite book
| last = Barber
| first = Charles
| title = In the Blood
| publisher = Grand Central Publishing
| location = New York
| year = 2023
| page = 123
}}</ref>

He is also the co-chair of the Scientific Advisory Board of the Institute of Bioengineering and Nanotechnology (IBN), [[A*STAR]], Singapore<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ibn.a-star.edu.sg/corporate_overview_04.php |title=Institute of Bioengineering and Nanotechnology |access-date=2008-02-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070916011143/http://www.ibn.a-star.edu.sg/corporate_overview_04.php |archive-date=September 16, 2007 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> which is headed by [[Jackie Y. Ying]] (Executive Director of IBN<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ibn.a-star.edu.sg/corporate_overview_01.php |title=Institute of Bioengineering and Nanotechnology |access-date=2008-02-22 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010122454/http://www.ibn.a-star.edu.sg/corporate_overview_01.php |archive-date=October 10, 2007 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> and adjunct professor of chemical engineering at MIT<ref>{{cite web|author=MIT – Department of Chemical Engineering |url=http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/ying.html |title=Jackie Y. Ying's profile at MIT |publisher=Web.mit.edu |access-date=December 17, 2011}}</ref>).

==Research group==
Alumni of Stucky's research group include [[Angela Belcher]] of MIT, [[Peidong Yang]] at UC Berkeley, [[Dongyuan Zhao]] at Fudan University, Yiying Wu at Ohio State, Kyong-Shin Choi at Wisconsin and [[Shannon W. Boettcher|Shannon Boettcher]] at the University of Oregon among many other notable scientists.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://belcher10.mit.edu/ |title=Biomolecular Materials Group at MIT |publisher=Belcher10.mit.edu |access-date=December 17, 2011 |archive-date=December 2, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111202023914/http://belcher10.mit.edu/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In late 2006, former and current group members and colleagues gathered for a Symposium on Recent Advances in Nanoscale Materials Research at UCSB to celebrate Stucky's 70th birthday.<ref>[http://www.cnsi.ucsb.edu/stucky/index.php Symposium on Recent Advances in Nanoscale Materials Research at UCSB, December 8, 2006]{{dead link|date=December 2011}}</ref> The event was hosted by CNSI (Elings Hall<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ia.ucsb.edu/pa/display.aspx?pkey=1610 |title=UCSB Receives $12.5 Million Gift from Virgil Elings and Betty Elings, 4 June 2007 |publisher=Ia.ucsb.edu |date=June 4, 2007 |access-date=December 17, 2011}}</ref>) at UCSB.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnsi.ucsb.edu |title=California NanoSystems Institute (Elings Hall), UCSB |publisher=Cnsi.ucsb.edu |access-date=December 17, 2011}}</ref>
